summary: Include verse 241 for the opening question.
rationale: The question “Hano yo u abre d ʕamməx?” occurs in 26/241. Verse 242 supplies the reply “E, ašər, hano yo ...”. The example combines both, so replacing 242 by 241 alone would lose the cited ašər reply.
The introductory “Mar, abre d ʕammo!” belongs to 26/213; the ašər promise to return her to her husband belongs to 26/214. Both verses are needed for the quoted exchange.

summary: Repeated ašər affirms a proposition or marks assurance, including inner speech and replies to 'in earnest?'. It is filed under III Imperativ following the inherited entry, without claiming productive command agreement in every occurrence.
Finite belief complements include a person marked with l- (existing Infectum example), a source with m- (59/37), pronominal content in 58/174, and an omitted proposition in MAC NE Samson the hero/15.

The Preterit question mašəllox expresses current conviction. Negative Infectum-wa in MAC NE Interview 2/187 concerns prospective belief under threat; the edition's 'hope' does not independently establish a new affective sense.
PrS 74/60 and PrS 86/45 duplicate the entry's page-based citations prs 215/20 and prs 256/9. The meal example also already exists. No duplicate added.

The inherited forms string and the cf. parenthesis inside sense 1 appear structurally irregular; they are preserved rather than silently repaired. Existing unnumbered examples are counted as unassigned in entry.md.
Is ašər synchronically an invariant assurance expression, and should it remain in the Imperativ box? Its occurrence in inner speech argues against treating every token as a literal command.
